newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals market loses momentum.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals market loses momentum.

text.p: The precious metals showed little enthusiasm on Monday for resuming last week's efforts to break out of a protracted downtrend, dealers said. "It's awfully quiet, the market is sleeping. There's no interest at all from investors or physical consumers," a London-based dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $381.05 an ounce, compared with $380.75 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $381.10/$381.60.
Dealers said prices were likely to remain stuck within a $378-$382.50 range for the time being, in the absence of clear market direction.
"The failure to overcome initial resistance at $383 and a turn around in silver helped to take the shine off gold, though prices are unlikely to seriously test support at $380," another dealer said.
Technical analysts, who study historical price charts, said gold still had the potential to eventually revisit recent lows around $377, and might dip still lower towards support at $370.
"We are beginning to feel gold is becoming susceptible to further selling pressure," analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary.
Strong bond and stock markets have dulled investor interest in gold, while demand for physical gold has been sparse as the jewellery industry awaits confirmation that prices have bottomed out.
Silver, which had posted the biggest move last week and shot above the psychological $5.00 level, was little changed from Friday's London close.
Prices were two cents higher at $5.03/$5.05 an ounce.
Sharp falls in silver warehouse stocks at New York's Comex futures market sparked a rally last week from 18-month lows.
Dealers said the metal was likely to consolidate within a $5.00-$5.10 range in the near term, although it showed more potential for further recovery than gold.
On the upside, silver needed to pierce resistance at around $5.15 an ounce in order to look constructive, dealers said.
Platinum was lower at $384.59/$385.50, down $1.00 from the London close, after making a stab at the key $390 resistance level last week. Palladium was down $0.75 at $117.00/$118.00.
Trading was expected to be low key in the U.S., where some U.S. markets would be closed for Columbus Day, although Comex would be open as usual.
